title: PutObject with ACL public-read fails with AccessControlListNotSupported on a new S3 bucket
symptoms: AccessControlListNotSupported: The bucket does not allow ACLs
400 on uploads that pass ACL: 'public-read' or --acl public-read
Same upload code works against an older bucket
cause: New buckets default to the Bucket owner enforced ownership setting, which disables ACLs. Any request that sets an ACL other than bucket-owner-full-control is rejected.
fix: Drop the ACL parameter and grant read access with a bucket policy or CloudFront instead. Only switch Object Ownership back to an ACL mode if you truly need per-object ACLs.
apply:
await s3.send(new PutObjectCommand({ Bucket, Key, Body, ContentType }));  // no ACL

# public read through a bucket policy (Block Public Access must allow it)
aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket my-bucket --policy '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":"*","Action":"s3:GetObject","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/*"}]}'
affected: S3 buckets created with default settings since the rollout that began 2023-04-05, which made Bucket owner enforced the default
